definitions.explanation: The time when the sky begins to lighten before sunrise; early morning twilight.
The early stages or beginning of something, especially a new era or movement.

examples.japanese: {曙|あけぼの}の{光|ひかり}が{差|さ}し{込|こ}む。
examples.english: The light of dawn streams in.
In spring, the dawn is lovely.
examples.notes: Famous opening line from {枕草子|まくらのそうし} (The Pillow Book).

examples.japanese: {新時代|しんじだい}の{曙|あけぼの}。
examples.english: The dawn of a new era.

examples.japanese: {文明|ぶんめい}の{曙|あけぼの}。
この{発見|はっけん}は{科学|かがく}{革命|かくめい}の{曙|あけぼの}となった。
examples.english: This discovery became the dawn of the scientific revolution.

notes:
{曙|あけぼの} is a poetic word for dawn.

LITERARY SIGNIFICANCE:
The word is famous from the opening of {枕草子|まくらのそうし} (The Pillow Book, ~1000 CE): {春|はる}は{曙|あけぼの} ("In spring, the dawn...").

REGISTER:
Poetic and literary; for everyday use, {夜明|よあ}け or {明|あ}け{方|がた} are more common.

RELATED:
- {暁|あかつき}: dawn (also literary)
- {夜明|よあ}け: daybreak (more common)
- {日|ひ}の{出|で}: sunrise
